title: process-canvas-and-approval-templates-2026
author: Nina Kapoor
body:
Overview

This page is a company-wide process canvas and template collection for the core operational domains: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. It combines: a lightweight process map (canvas), standard approval flows, SLA expectations, and downloadable templates (request forms, decision checklists, and vendor intake). Use this as the canonical starting point for operational requests that cross teams.

Goals

- Reduce ambiguity about who approves what and how long approvals should take.
- Centralize minimal required artifacts so audits and reviews complete quickly.
- Provide reusable templates that reduce back-and-forth and enable measurable SLAs.

When to use this document

- You are introducing a new third-party vendor, requesting elevated access, initiating a production change, purchasing non-routine hardware/software, or booking extended business travel.
- Use the specific template linked in each section; incomplete forms are rejected and returned for clarification.

Process canvas (high level)

1) Initiate: Requester fills the relevant template (Access Request, Change Request, Purchase Request, Vendor Intake, Travel Authorization).
2) Triage: Owner team (People Ops / IT / Procurement / Security) validates completeness within 24 business hours.
3) Review: Required reviewers (Security, Legal, Finance, Service Owner) evaluate and comment within the SLA window.
4) Decision: Approve / Approve with conditions / Reject. Decision recorded in the ticket and archive.
5) Execute: Implementer performs work; implementer updates ticket and attaches evidence (logs, receipts, deployed commit IDs).
6) Close & Audit: Owner team verifies execution artifacts and closes the request; data retained per retention schedule.

RACI snapshot (default for cross-functional ops)

- Requester: R
- Owner team (triage and archival): A
- Security: C for access/vendor/change; A for security-only approvals
- Legal: C for vendor contracts, restricted data use
- Finance: C for procurement and budgets, A for purchase approvals > $50k
- Service Owner / Engineering: C for production changes, A for production rollout approvals

Access and permissions

Purpose: Standardize onboarding, role changes, and elevated access (privileged roles).

Key requirements

- All access requests must use the Access Request template (link: Access Request form).
- Requests must identify: system(s), exact roles, justification, business owner, and expiration date.
- Temporary elevated access is limited to 30 days unless documented business need and explicit Security approval.
- MFA is mandatory for all privileged accounts; proof of MFA enrollment required for approval.

Approval flow

1) Submit Access Request -> 24h triage by IT.
2) Security review within 48h (risk assessment: low/medium/high).
3) Business owner approves (SLA 72h).
4) IT implements and documents the change with ticket ID and timestamp.

Change management (production changes)

Scope: Any change to production code, infra, or configuration that could affect availability, correctness, or cost.

Change categories

- Standard (pre-approved routine operations, e.g., config toggles below threshold)
- Minor (low risk code/config updates with rollback plan)
- Major (changes touching stateful services, schema migrations, or cross-region infra)

Mandatory checklist for Minor and Major changes

- Change Request template completed with: rollback plan, monitoring checklist, SLOs impacted, deployment window, and test plan.
- Pre-approval from Service Owner and an on-call engineer.
- Security and Compliance review for Major changes.

Deployment windows and SLAs

- Standard changes: can be scheduled in weekly maintenance windows; no immediate review required.
- Minor changes: 48h review SLA.
- Major changes: 5 business days for review; emergency exceptions allowed with post-facto RCA and exception logging.

Data management

Principles

- Least privilege and data minimization are default.
- Data classification must be applied at ingestion (Public/Internal/Confidential/Restricted).
- PII and regulated data require documented storage locations and access controls.

Operational rules

- Data retention policy: default retention 2 years for logs, 7 years for financial records, configurable retention applied at dataset creation.
- Backups: daily incremental + weekly full for critical datasets; test recovery quarterly.
- Data deletion requests use the Data Deletion template and require product and legal sign-off for Confidential/Restricted datasets.

Procurement and expenses

Policy highlights

- Routine purchases (< $5k): teams may approve locally; expense reports required within 30 days.
- Non-routine purchases ($5k–$50k): Procurement review and Finance approval required.
- Capital and contract-level purchases (> $50k): Procurement + Finance + Executive sponsor sign-off; multi-year contracts routed to Legal for review.

Purchase request flow

1) Submit Purchase Request (itemized quote, budget code, business justification).
2) Procurement triage within 48h.
3) Finance verifies available budget (72h).
4) Legal review for contracts > $25k (5 business days).

Expense reimbursement rules

- Acceptable receipts: itemized invoices or electronic receipts.
- Per diem: set by Geography tab in Travel Policy (use sample table below).
- Credit card reconciliation: monthly; missing receipts escalate to manager review.

Vendor management

Third-party intake checklist

- Vendor Intake form completed with: product description, data flows, subprocessors, security posture, compliance certifications (SOC2/ISO27001), and contract term.
- Security to run a risk evaluation for data access.
- Legal to negotiate standard security & privacy clauses; use Contract Appendix A (Data Processing Addendum) for vendors processing personal data.

Ongoing vendor controls

- Quarterly review for strategic vendors; annual security re-evaluation for vendors with access to Restricted data.
- Termination playbook: revoke credentials, collect assets, attest to data deletion or return.

Travel and remote work expenses

Authorization steps

1) Travel Authorization form for trips > 2 nights or requiring > $2k budget.
2) Manager and People Ops approval prior to booking.

Booking and per-diem table (examples)

| Region | Max hotel/night (USD) | Per diem/day (USD) | Notes |
|--------|-----------------------:|-------------------:|-------|
| North America (US/CA) | 250 | 75 | Higher cost metros require pre-approval |
| Europe | 220 | 70 | Use company travel portal where available |
| APAC | 200 | 65 | Some markets have lower caps; check local policy |

Templates and examples (downloadable)

Included templates (canonical):

- Access Request form (fields: requester, system, role, business owner, justification, expiration)
- Change Request template (fields: owner, description, rollout plan, rollback, test checklist, monitoring)
- Purchase Request form (fields: vendor, itemized quote, budget code, procurement reason)
- Vendor Intake form (fields: product, data processed, subprocessors, certifications)
- Travel Authorization & Expense Report template (fields: itinerary, purpose, per-diem, receipts)
- Data Deletion request template (fields: dataset id, retention justification, product owner sign-off)

Example: minimal Access Request (copy into ticket)

```
Title: Temporary S3 read access for onboarding contractor
Requester: Jane Doe (Platform)
System: S3://redwood-prod-logs
Role: read-only (list/get)
Business owner: Platform Infra (owner: Miguel Ortega)
Justification: Contractor will run log-parsing job for 2 weeks
Expiration: 2025-11-28
```

Escalation and exceptions

- If an SLA is missed by the owner team, the request auto-escalates to their manager after 48 business hours.
- Emergency exceptions (production outage changes, urgent vendor patching) must include a post-action RCA and documented approvals within 72 hours of the emergency action.

Audit artifacts and retention

- All templates and approvals should be captured in the ticketing system (Jira or Zendesk depending on team).
- Audit exports: Procurement and Security keep a quarterly export of approvals for audit teams.
- Retention: approvals and contracts retained per Finance retention schedule (minimum 7 years for contracts).

Ownership and maintenance of this page

- Primary owner: People Ops (Nina Kapoor).
- Technical reviewer: Security (Ethan Morales).
- Content review cadence: annual; after material changes to procurement thresholds, security requirements, or legislation.

Appendix A — Quick approvals matrix

- Access Requests (normal): IT triage 24h, Security 48h, Business owner 72h
- Purchases <$5k: Local manager approval -> Procurement notified
- Purchases $5k–$50k: Procurement + Finance (3 business days)
- Purchases >$50k: Procurement + Finance + Exec sponsor + Legal (up to 10 business days)

Appendix B — Useful links

- Access Request form: /confluence/forms/access-request
- Change Request template: /confluence/templates/change-request
- Vendor intake & DPA: /confluence/security-and-compliance/vendor-onboarding
- Expense submission: /confluence/finance/expense-workflow
